hook.en: Air is essential but free; a diamond is not essential but costly. Why? To answer, we need the words goods, utility, value and price.

objectives.en: Classify goods as free or economic, consumer or capital, intermediate or final
Explain utility, value in use and value in exchange
Define price, wealth, income and money

narration.en: Air is essential but free; a diamond is not essential but costly. Why? To answer, we need the words goods, utility, value and price.

body.en: Goods are things that satisfy human wants. Free goods, like air, are given by nature in plenty and have no price; economic goods are scarce and command a price. Consumer goods satisfy wants directly; capital goods, like machines, help produce other goods. Utility is the want-satisfying power of a good. It is subjective, depends on the intensity of the want and is not the same as usefulness: a cigarette has utility for a smoker. Marginal utility, the addition to total utility from one more unit, usually falls as more is consumed.

points.en: Consumer goods vs capital goods; intermediate vs final
Total utility = sum of marginal utilities

title.en: Value, price, wealth, income and money

body.en: Value in use is the utility of a good; value in exchange is the quantity of other goods it can command. Water has high value in use but low value in exchange; a diamond the reverse, because it is scarce. Value in exchange expressed in money is price. Wealth is the stock of goods that have utility, are scarce, are transferable and can be valued in money. Income is a flow of earnings over a period. Money is anything generally accepted as a medium of exchange and a measure of value.

points.en: Price = value in exchange expressed in money
Wealth is a stock; income is a flow
Money: medium of exchange, measure of value, store of value
